items.note: Full-width teal band with breadcrumb, regular-weight 'Profile' h1, ink-on-band subtitle and pill sub-nav whose selected pill is white raised; below, one outlined raised card with a two-column form, a teal initials tile and a save row with one pink 'Save changes' plus a ghost 'Reset'.

The band collapses to the title, subtitle and a sideways-scrolling pill strip (the 'Billing' pill cut off at the edge signals the scroll); the form stacks into one column inside the outlined card, with the pink save and ghost reset kept in the flow.

Same layout on a black ground: the teal band keeps ink text, the selected pill flips to a dark fill, the card is the raised dark gray with a light border, and pink stays the only filled action (Save changes).
Single-column form in a raised dark card under the teal band and pill strip; inputs have light outlines, and the pink save sits next to the outlined reset with good contrast throughout.

Teal band with h1, a '3 of 6 notifications on' status pill and pill sub-nav; two outlined cards (Email, Push notifications) list rows split by hairline rules, each with an On/Off word next to a switch. Switches that are on are filled ink, not pink, because the spec contradicts itself on this.

The two cards stack full-width under the collapsed band; every row wraps its description cleanly with the On/Off label and switch on the right, nothing cramped. The ink on-switches carry the same spec contradiction.

Dark raised cards on black, light hairlines between rows, and on-switches drawn as a light fill with a dark knob; the band keeps ink text and the status pill is a dark selected pill. The on-switch color has the same spec contradiction.
Stacked dark cards with readable row titles and secondary descriptions, On/Off words next to every switch so the state isn't shown by color alone; same switch-color contradiction as in light mode.

A Change password card with three outlined inputs, a hint line and one pink 'Update password', then an 'Active sessions' table in a bordered box with a gray header, a 'This device' pill and outlined Revoke row actions with an icon.

The password card reflows to full-width inputs, but the sessions table keeps its desktop columns. Only Device and Location show, the location text touches the right border, and every Revoke action and the Last active column are off-screen with no scroll cue.

Dark version of the security page: raised dark password card with a pink submit, sessions table with light rules, and Revoke actions drawn as outlined dark buttons with a red-tinted icon next to the word.
Same truncated sessions table in dark: the Device and Location columns fill the box and the Revoke actions can't be seen without swiping inside the table, so the screen's main task is hidden.

Three outlined plan cards with pink price tags (the current plan marked by a darker border and a 'Current plan' status pill, the others with ghost switch buttons), a Payment method card and an invoices table with tabular amounts and outlined Due/Paid status pills with icons.
Plan cards stack full-width with even 16px-ish gaps, then the payment card and a four-column invoices table that fits the 390px box without sideways scroll; pink appears only as small price tags.
Dark raised plan cards with pink price tags kept, a light border marking the current plan, a dark payment card and an invoices table whose Due pill uses an amber icon next to the word.
Stacked dark plan cards, payment card and a compact invoices table that fits; the band's selected 'Billing' pill is a dark fill, and all text has strong contrast on the black ground.

findings.summary: Still not fixed from the previous review: at phone width, the active-sessions table keeps its desktop columns and scrolls sideways inside its box with no cue. Only Device and Location show, the location text runs into the right border, and every Revoke row action and the Last active column are off-screen, in light and dark.
findings.promptFix: Under breakpoint.md, a table whose rows have actions never hides them behind sideways scroll. Reflow each row into a stacked block inside the same bordered box: the primary cell as its title, the other cells as label/value lines, and the row action visible at the end of the block. Sideways scroll inside the box is only for read-only tables, and then the last visible column must be cut part-way to show there is more, with space.12 of padding so no cell text touches the border. Verify at 390px that every row action is visible without scrolling the table.

findings.summary: The spec contradicts itself about switches that are on. The Interaction table says a selected checkbox or switch is filled with color.action.primary, but 'Never' and 'Color use' forbid a pink selected control or toggle. The build drew on-switches in ink (paper in dark), so they no longer echo the pink selected-dot accent and the rule is decided by guesswork.
